Design a detailed, phased implementation plan for a large new feature area in the Nxeon codebase (/opt/nxeon — Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Prisma, Postgres). This is PRODUCTION work (not the sandbox), for a real business that just hired its first employee (marketing + customer support). Do not write any code — this is planning only. Read whatever files you need to confirm exact patterns before proposing changes.

## The ask (from the business owner)

1. A separate, dedicated employee portal (distinct from both the customer dashboard and the existing owner/admin portal at /admin) for staff to work in.
2. Per-employee custom permission grants — the owner picks exactly which pages/tools each individual employee can access, not fixed roles. For the first employee: Support tickets, the Reddit template library, the company Inbox + Mailboxes, and a NEW minimal/limited read-only Clients view (no financials, no IP history, no audit log, no impersonate — just name/email/signup date/ticket count/server count).
3. All staff (including this one) managed from the existing /admin portal — i.e. admin/owner keeps the full admin portal, and gets a new "Staff" management area there to create employees, assign their permission grants, and configure IP whitelisting.
4. Per-employee IP whitelist, enforced when logging into/using the employee portal.
5. A "ClickUp alternative" — a real project/task management system (Kanban boards + to-do lists + more) usable by BOTH admin and staff, with admin able to fully monitor/oversee everything staff do in it. Plus a request to brainstorm what else belongs in this area (recurring tasks, time tracking, task templates, calendar view, notifications, etc. — the owner explicitly asked "what are some other things we can do in this area?").
6. Admin should be able to see ALL actions staff perform anywhere in the system (comprehensive activity/audit visibility, not just within the task manager).

## Ground truth from prior investigation (already done, trust this — don't re-derive from scratch, but verify specifics by reading the actual files before finalizing the plan)

**Current RBAC** (`/opt/nxeon/lib/rbac.ts`, `/opt/nxeon/lib/auth.ts`, `/opt/nxeon/prisma/schema.prisma`):
- `Role` enum: `CUSTOMER | SUPPORT | BILLING | ADMIN`. No per-user permission storage on `User` today — access is computed from `role` alone.
- `lib/rbac.ts` defines 8 fixed `Area` values (`overview, analytics, clients, support, fleet, billing, accounting, platform`) and a static `AREA_ROLES: Record<Area, Role[]>` map. `canAccess(role, area)` and `requireArea(area)` (redirects if not allowed) are used at ~85 admin page files and ~30 action files, almost always as the first line, often re-checked per-action (defense in depth).
- **Critically**, `platform` is an ADMIN-only catch-all bucket containing Reddit templates, the company Inbox, Mailboxes, Settings, Staff, Audit log, cold-email, marketing-drafts, ads, agency, SEO, domains — everything not already split into overview/analytics/clients/support/fleet/billing/accounting. This is the reason today's system can't grant "just Reddit + Inbox + Mailboxes" — the plan needs to split `platform` into finer areas OR (better, per the owner's per-employee-grant answer below) move past the role→area model entirely for staff.
- `lib/admin-groups.ts`'s `ADMIN_NAV` + `HREF_AREA` in `lib/rbac.ts` are the single source of truth mapping every admin route to its area, for both nav visibility and route guards — any new grantable page needs an entry here.
- A previous attempt at finer customer-team-permission granularity (`lib/team-guard.ts`, a per-org `requireArea(orgId, area)`) was **deliberately deleted** because it only filtered nav without real server-side enforcement on actions — treated as a security regression, ripped out rather than left half-done. Learn from this: any new grant system MUST be enforced at the server-action layer, never just nav-level.
- Action-layer gates are inconsistent today: some files call `requireArea(...)`, some call `requireAdmin()` directly (bypassing area logic — e.g. `lib/actions-reddit-templates.ts`), some check `isStaff(role)` (broader, e.g. the IMAP mail layer `lib/mail/imap.ts`'s `resolveMailbox()`). A new grant system needs a single new gating primitive that all relevant actions get migrated to, not just the pages.
- Impersonation is a real, working, separate mechanism (`lib/auth.ts`) — session vs impersonation vs any future "staff portal session" should stay cleanly distinguished (existing pattern: distinct JWT `typ` discriminators for session vs impersonation tokens).
- IP restriction today: only ONE global admin-portal-wide allowlist (`allowed_admin_ips` setting, checked in `app/admin/layout.tsx`'s `adminIpBlocked()`, fails OPEN if unset/malformed). No per-user IP list anywhere. `lib/rate-limit.ts` has a reusable `clientIp()`/IP-extraction primitive already used elsewhere (trusts `X-Real-IP`/`X-Forwarded-For` from nginx).
- `NXEON_ADMIN_HOSTS` env var + `adminHostBlocked()` in `app/admin/layout.tsx` already 404s `/admin` entirely unless the request Host header matches — i.e. the admin portal is ALREADY expected to live on its own dedicated hostname, distinct from the public site. This is useful precedent/scaffolding for standing up a new, separately-hosted employee portal.
- `AuditLog` model (`userId?`, `action: String`, `detail?: String`, `createdAt`) exists with a real viewer at `/opt/nxeon/app/admin/audit/page.tsx` (`requireArea("platform")`, shows latest 200 rows, resolves an `actingAdmin=<id>` marker embedded in `detail` for impersonation attribution). BUT: the `audit()` helper in `lib/actions.ts` is private/unexported and only used by ~5 call sites in that one file; most other `lib/actions-*.ts` files do their own direct `db.auditLog.create(...)` calls ad hoc — coverage is inconsistent, not a codebase-wide enforced convention. A real "see everything staff do" feature needs a SHARED, exported audit helper that gets threaded through every staff-reachable action (both existing ones being newly opened to staff, and the new task-system actions), not a continuation of the current scattered pattern.

**The five specific admin surfaces this employee needs, and their current shape**:
1. **Support tickets** — `/opt/nxeon/app/admin/support/page.tsx` + `/opt/nxeon/app/admin/support/[id]/page.tsx`, actions in `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-support.ts` (a local `requireTicketActor()` helper checks `canAccess(role, "support")`). Already `SUPPORT`+`ADMIN` reachable via the existing `support` area — reuse as-is once staff's new role/grant maps to this area. No code-level "reply requires a second human's sign-off" gate exists (that's a separate, unrelated standing rule for how *you*, the AI assistant, behave in your own work — not a requirement to build a staff approval workflow; do not build a ticket-reply approval queue unless explicitly asked).
2. **Reddit templates** — `/opt/nxeon/app/admin/reddit/page.tsx` (page-gated `requireArea("platform")`, needs moving to a new area), actions in `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-reddit-templates.ts` (each action calls `requireAdmin()` directly — needs migrating to the new grant check too, not just the page). Low-risk, static content only (categories/subreddits/templates), no live posting, no customer data.
3. **Company Inbox** — `/opt/nxeon/app/admin/inbox/page.tsx` — in-admin webmail for company addresses (admin@/support@/etc, NOT customer mail, NOT the unrelated cold-email outreach inbox at `/admin/coldemail/inbox` which is a different, unrelated feature backed by a differently-purposed `Inbox` Prisma model — don't confuse the two). Page-gated `requireArea("platform")`. The underlying `resolveMailbox()` (`/opt/nxeon/lib/mail/imap.ts`) already accepts any `isStaff()` role for company mailboxes — so opening this up is mostly a page-gate change.
4. **Company Mailboxes management** — `/opt/nxeon/app/admin/mailboxes/page.tsx`, actions in `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-company-mail.ts` (consistently `requireArea("platform")` today, needs migrating to new area/grant). Manages the `CompanyMailbox` model — create/reveal-password/reset-password/delete for admin@/support@ style addresses. No customer billing/PII. (The owner explicitly wants COMPANY mailboxes, not customer email-hosting — confirmed.)
5. **NEW minimal Clients view** — does not exist today; today's only client list/detail (`/opt/nxeon/app/admin/users/page.tsx` + `[id]/page.tsx`, area `clients`) is a full "customer 360" exposing wallet balance, lifetime spend, invoices, transactions, IP/geolocation history, audit trail, internal notes — confirmed explicitly too much for this hire (the owner chose the "build a new minimal view" option). This needs a genuinely NEW, separate page/route (not a stripped-down version of the existing one reusing its data-fetching — avoid the temptation to just hide fields client-side; the SERVER query itself for this new view should only ever select name/email/signup-date/ticket-count/server-count, so no sensitive data reaches the page payload at all, matching the "a control a role cannot use is not a permission, it is a promise the server refuses to keep" principle already documented in this codebase's own `/admin/users` page comment).

**Existing internal Kanban board** (`Board`/`BoardColumn`/`Card`/`CardAttachment`/`CardComment` in schema, `/opt/nxeon/app/admin/board/page.tsx`, `/opt/nxeon/components/admin/BoardClient.tsx`, `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-board.ts`) is ADMIN-ONLY by hard `requireAdmin()` at every layer, and has a bespoke "execution pipeline" feature wired to card movement that spawns real deploy/git scripts (`runCardStageAction` — publish-docs.mjs, deploy-staging.sh, promote-production.sh) — this is Nxeon's own internal dev-ops roadmap tool, NOT suitable as the base for a general staff task-management system (the deploy-script triggering must never be reachable by non-admin staff). Reusable patterns from it: the `App→Board→BoardColumn→Card` hierarchy shape, `CardType`/`CardPriority` enums, hand-rolled native-HTML5-drag-and-drop Kanban UI (no DnD library currently installed — `dnd-kit` would be a new, reasonable, small dependency if a nicer drag experience is wanted), attachment-on-disk-plus-metadata-row pattern, full-list-renumber position strategy. NOT reusable as-is: `Card.assignee` is free-text, not a `User` relation; no due dates; no checklists/sub-items; `CardComment.authorName` is a text snapshot, not a real `User` FK — a proper task system needs its own parallel model set with real `assigneeId` FKs, due dates, and a checklist/sub-item child model, kept structurally separate from `Card` so the deploy-pipeline feature can never leak into it.

**Owner's answers to clarifying questions** (already decided, build the plan around these):
- Employee portal: a genuinely SEPARATE, dedicated portal (own nav/look), not just a permission-filtered version of /admin.
- Permission model: fully custom PER-EMPLOYEE grants (a checklist of grantable pages/areas per individual staff member), not fixed named roles.
- Clients view for limited-access staff: a NEW minimal read-only view (name/email/signup date/ticket count/server count only).
- Mailboxes: company mailboxes (admin@/support@ style), paired with Inbox — not customer email hosting.

## What I need from you

A concrete, phased implementation plan covering:

1. **Data model changes** — exact new Prisma models/fields needed for: per-employee permission grants (a flexible, page/area-keyed grant table — design its shape given the "per-employee custom checklist" requirement, considering how it interacts with the existing `Area` enum/`AREA_ROLES` system: extend the `Area` union with finer values by splitting `platform`, and add a new user-level grant table that ADDS to or REPLACES the role-based area check for staff, your call on which is cleaner given the codebase's existing patterns), per-employee IP whitelist (one or more allowed IPs/CIDRs per user), and the new task-management system's models (tasks/lists/boards usable by staff+admin, real `assigneeId` FK to `User`, due dates, priority, checklist/sub-item child model, comments with real `authorId`, activity logging). Reuse existing enums (`CardType`/`CardPriority`-equivalent) where sensible rather than reinventing.

2. **RBAC/auth changes** — how `lib/rbac.ts`/`lib/auth.ts` need to change to support per-user grants layered on top of (or replacing, for staff) the existing role→area model, without breaking the existing ADMIN/SUPPORT/BILLING/CUSTOMER behavior for everything already working today. Propose the exact new gating primitive (e.g. a `requireGrant(area)` or similar) that new AND existing actions should call, and be explicit about migrating the specific action files identified above (Reddit's `requireAdmin()` calls, Mailboxes/Inbox's `requireArea("platform")` calls) to the new system without regressing today's ADMIN-only protection for the OTHER tools still bundled under `platform` (Settings, Staff management itself, Audit log, cold-email, ads, agency — these must stay ADMIN-only unless the owner explicitly grants them to someone).

3. **Employee portal** — where it lives (new route group under a new host, e.g. reusing `NXEON_ADMIN_HOSTS`-style host-gating for a THIRD dedicated hostname alongside the customer site and admin portal), how staff log in (same unified login+session as today, per the existing pattern — NOT a new auth system), how its nav is built dynamically from each staff member's actual grants (never hardcoded), and per-employee IP whitelist enforcement (where to check it — likely mirroring `adminIpBlocked()`'s pattern but per-user, and needs a decision on fail-open-if-unset vs fail-closed-once-configured — recommend fail-closed once an admin has added at least one IP for that specific employee, fail-open/unrestricted if they've never configured one, to avoid accidental lockouts from an empty list).

4. **Admin-side Staff management UI** — a new "Staff" area (already reserved as an admin-groups entry `/admin/staff` per the exploration, though not yet built out to this scope) letting the owner: invite/create employee accounts, check off their exact page/area grants from a list, configure their IP whitelist, view their activity. Must itself be ADMIN-only (never staff-manageable by other staff).

5. **The "ClickUp alternative" project/task system** — propose a concrete MVP feature set (boards/lists, kanban columns, real task assignment, due dates, priority, checklists, comments, file attachments) PLUS a clearly-separated "future ideas" list answering the owner's open "what else belongs here" question (e.g. recurring tasks, time tracking/estimates, calendar/timeline view, per-task notifications, task templates, personal to-do lists distinct from team boards, workload/velocity dashboards, saved filters/views, @mentions). Design it so admin has full, real-time visibility into everything staff create/move/comment/complete (reusing the shared audit helper from point 6), without staff being able to see/access the unrelated internal dev-ops board.

6. **Comprehensive staff activity visibility** — design a SINGLE shared, exported audit helper (replacing the inconsistent private/ad-hoc pattern) that every staff-reachable action (both newly-opened existing ones and new task-system ones) is migrated to call, plus enhancements to the existing `/admin/audit` viewer (e.g. filter by specific staff member) so the owner can see "everything employee X did" in one place.

## Constraints to respect in the plan

- This is PRODUCTION code (`/opt/nxeon`), not the sandbox. The plan should note the existing deploy workflow (commit → `deploy-staging.sh` → `promote-production.sh`) and that this work should be built/tested on staging before promotion, given its security-sensitive nature (a mistake here could over-expose customer data to a limited-access employee).
- No existing ADMIN/SUPPORT/BILLING/CUSTOMER behavior may regress — every migration of an existing gate (Reddit, Mailboxes, Inbox) must preserve today's ADMIN-only protection for every OTHER tool currently bundled under `platform`.
- Follow the codebase's own established discipline: no half-wired permission UI (nav-only filtering without real server-side enforcement) — the `lib/team-guard.ts` deletion is a hard lesson already learned here, cite it as precedent to avoid repeating.
- No new external dependencies unless clearly justified (e.g. `dnd-kit` for the task board's drag-and-drop, if you think it's warranted over hand-rolling native drag events again).

Produce a clear, phased plan (this is a large epic — organize it into logical phases with a sensible build order, e.g. data model + RBAC foundation first, then admin staff-management UI, then employee portal shell, then the five granted tools wired through, then the task-management system, then audit/activity polish). For each phase, name the critical files to create/modify. Do not write actual code — describe the approach precisely enough that a future implementation pass can execute it directly.

# Nxeon Employee Portal, Per-Employee Permissions, and Task Management — Implementation Plan

## Summary of key architectural decisions (read this first)

Before the phases, the decisions that shape everything else, made after reading the actual code:

1. **New `Role` enum value: `EMPLOYEE`** (not `STAFF`) — deliberately different from the existing `isStaff()` helper name. `isStaff()` in `/opt/nxeon/lib/rbac.ts` today means exactly `SUPPORT | BILLING | ADMIN` and is checked in ~8 files; naming the new role `STAFF` would make `isStaff(EMPLOYEE_USER.role) === false` read as a bug to every future engineer. `EMPLOYEE` avoids the trap. `isStaff()` itself is **not** changed — this is the main lever that keeps the blast radius small.

2. **Additive, not a replacement.** `Role.CUSTOMER/SUPPORT/BILLING/ADMIN` keep working exactly as today, through the existing `AREA_ROLES` map in `lib/rbac.ts`, completely untouched. A new parallel mechanism — a per-user `StaffGrant` table plus a new async helper module `lib/staff-grants.ts` — governs `EMPLOYEE`-role users only. `Role.EMPLOYEE` is never listed in `AREA_ROLES` for any area, so an `EMPLOYEE` gets *zero* access anywhere until a grant row exists for them. `canAccess()` and `requireArea()` in `lib/rbac.ts` are not modified, so all ~85 page files and ~30 action files that already call them are untouched and provably unaffected.

3. **`Area` union gets new, narrow members, not a wholesale re-slicing of `platform`.** I confirmed by grepping that `requireArea("platform")` is called from 14+ unrelated action files (`actions-broadcast.ts`, `actions-ads.ts`, `actions-agency.ts`, `actions-seo.ts`, `actions-coldemail*.ts`, etc.) that must stay ADMIN-only forever. So instead of restructuring `platform`, I carve out **exactly** the new areas needed and leave `platform` and its other ~25 routes completely alone:
   - `redditTemplates` (was folded into `platform`)
   - `companyInbox` (was folded into `platform`)
   - `companyMailboxes` (was folded into `platform`)
   - `clientsBasic` (brand new, no existing route uses it)
   - `supportTickets` (brand new and **narrower than the existing `support` area** — see point 4)
   - `tasks` (brand new, for the project/task system)

4. **`support` is deliberately *not* touched or split**, even though "Support tickets" is one of the four requested tools. I found that the existing `support` area is shared by far more than the ticket queue: live chat (`lib/actions-chat.ts`, 9 call sites), the Discord support bridge (`lib/discord-oauth.ts`, `lib/actions-discord-link.ts`, `lib/discord-bridge.ts`, three `app/api/admin/discord/*` routes), feedback (`lib/actions-feedback.ts`), two unread-count API routes, and a dedicated structural test (`test/discord-oauth-guards.test.ts`) that hardcodes the literal strings `requireArea("support")` and `canAccess(me.role, "support")`. Renaming or splitting `support` itself would touch ~15 files and one test file for zero benefit. Instead, I introduce a **new, narrower** area, `supportTickets`, used *only* by the two ticket pages and the ticket-actor helper — chat/feedback/Discord keep using the original `support` area, completely unaffected, and remain unreachable by `EMPLOYEE` role forever (unless a future phase explicitly decides to extend grants there).

5. **The gating primitive migration lesson from `lib/team-guard.ts`'s deletion is treated as binding.** Every area opened to `EMPLOYEE` gets its **server action** re-gated (not just its page), using one new exported primitives-pair (`requireGrant` / `requireAreaOrGrant`) in `lib/staff-grants.ts`. No page-only filtering is acceptable anywhere in this plan.

6. **This codebase enforces RBAC with literal structural tests, not just convention** — this is important and must shape execution order. I found:
   - `test/company-mailbox.test.ts` hardcodes `requireArea('platform')` as a regex against every export of `lib/actions-company-mail.ts`, hardcodes `isStaff(user.role)` inside `resolveMailbox`, and hardcodes `"/admin/mailboxes": "platform"` in `lib/rbac.ts`.
   - `test/admin-actions-guards.test.ts` has a fixed `AUTH_MARKERS`/`STAFF_MARKERS` allowlist of guard-call substrings and a fixed `ADMIN_ACTION_FILES` list.
   - `test/customer-actions-guards.test.ts` allowlists `requireTicketActor(` by name with a comment describing its current internal implementation.
   
   Every phase below that changes a gate **must** update the matching test assertions in the same commit — this is a feature of the repo (it will catch a real regression), not friction to route around.

---

## Phase 1 — Data model foundation (schema only, purely additive)

No behavior changes yet. All new fields nullable/new tables, safe for `npm run db:push` ahead of any code that depends on them, consistent with the schema's existing "stage the column before the code needs it" discipline (see the `discordUserId` comment in `prisma/schema.prisma`).

**Prisma schema changes (`/opt/nxeon/prisma/schema.prisma`):**

- `enum Role`: add `EMPLOYEE`.
- New model `StaffGrant`: `id`, `userId` (FK → `User`, cascade delete), `area` (plain `String`, **not** a Postgres enum — validated against the `Area` TS union in code, matching this schema's own established convention for fast-changing value sets, e.g. the `AuditLog`/`Expense.category` comment block explaining why those are `String` instead of a native enum), `createdById` (nullable, which admin granted it, for audit), `createdAt`. `@@unique([userId, area])`, `@@index([userId])`.
- New model `StaffIpAllow`: `id`, `userId` (FK, cascade), `cidr` (`String` — literal IPv4/IPv6 or IPv4 CIDR, normalized at write time), `label` (nullable), `createdAt`. `@@index([userId])`. (Deliberately a *list* of rows per user, not a comma-joined string like the global `allowed_admin_ips` setting, since per-user CRUD — add one IP, remove one IP — is a first-class UI operation here, unlike the rarely-touched global list.)
- New models for the task system, named with a `Work` prefix specifically so they can never be confused with or accidentally wired into the existing dev-ops `Board`/`Card` tables (whose `runCardStageAction` triggers real deploy scripts and must never become reachable by `EMPLOYEE`-role users):
  - `WorkBoard`: `id`, `name`, `description`, `archivedAt?`, `createdById` (FK → `User`), `createdAt`.
  - `WorkColumn`: `id`, `boardId` (FK, cascade), `name`, `position`.
  - `WorkTask`: `id`, `boardId` (FK, cascade), `columnId` (FK, cascade), `title`, `description` (markdown, default `""`), `priority` (reuse the existing `CardPriority` enum — `LOW|NORMAL|HIGH|URGENT` — rather than inventing a new one, per the instruction to reuse where sensible), `assigneeId?` (**real** FK → `User`, `onDelete: SetNull` — this is the key structural fix vs. the old `Card.assignee` free-text field), `dueAt?` (`DateTime?`, new — the old `Card` has no due date), `position`, `archivedAt?`, `completedAt?`, `createdById` (FK → `User`), `createdAt`, `updatedAt`.
  - `WorkChecklistItem`: `id`, `taskId` (FK, cascade), `label`, `done` (`Boolean @default(false)`), `position`, `createdAt` — the sub-item model the old `Card` never had.
  - `WorkTaskComment`: `id`, `taskId` (FK, cascade), `authorId` (**real** FK → `User` — fixes `CardComment.authorName`'s text-snapshot problem), `body`, `createdAt`.
  - `WorkTaskAttachment`: `id`, `taskId` (FK, cascade), `filename`, `storedName`, `mime`, `sizeBytes`, `kind` (reuse existing `AttachmentKind` enum), `uploadedById` (FK → `User`), `createdAt`.
  - Indexes: `@@index([boardId])`/`@@index([columnId])` on `WorkTask`, `@@index([assigneeId])` on `WorkTask` (for "my tasks" queries), `@@index([taskId])` on the three child tables.
  - Deliberately **no** `WorkBoardMember`/per-board ACL table in this phase — MVP scope is "any `tasks`-granted user sees every board." Noted as a Phase-6 future idea, not built now.

**Critical files this phase touches:** `/opt/nxeon/prisma/schema.prisma` only. Run `npm run db:push` on staging first, then `npx prisma generate`, per the project's existing db-push (not migrate) workflow.

---

## Phase 2 — RBAC gating primitive + migrating the four existing tools' gates

**New file `/opt/nxeon/lib/staff-grants.ts`** (kept separate from `lib/rbac.ts` so the ~85+30 existing call sites of `canAccess`/`requireArea` are provably untouched):

- `hasAreaAccess(user: {id,role}, area: Area): Promise<boolean>` — fast path: `canAccess(user.role, area)` (unchanged legacy check, covers ADMIN/SUPPORT/BILLING instantly, no DB hit for them). Only if `user.role === "EMPLOYEE"` does it fall through to a `db.staffGrant.findUnique({ where: { userId_area: { userId, area } } })` lookup.
- `hasAnyAreaAccess(user, areas: Area[]): Promise<boolean>` — OR-logic, needed because `listCompanyMailboxes`/`listCompanyMailboxInfos` are called from *both* the Inbox and Mailboxes pages and must be reachable by either grant.
- `requireGrant(area: Area): Promise<User>` — throws `FORBIDDEN`/`UNAUTHORIZED`; for server actions. Rejects `CUSTOMER` outright; otherwise defers to `hasAreaAccess`.
- `requireAnyGrant(areas: Area[]): Promise<User>` — action-layer OR-variant.
- `requireAreaOrGrant(area: Area): Promise<User>` — redirects (mirrors `requireArea`'s page-guard shape exactly, so it's a drop-in replacement in page files); redirects `EMPLOYEE` without the grant to `/staff`, everyone else without access to `/admin` (or `/dashboard` if not staff at all), matching `requireArea`'s existing redirect conventions.
- `listGrantedAreas(userId): Promise<Area[]>` — used to build the employee portal's dynamic nav (Phase 4) and the admin grant-checklist UI (Phase 3).

**`lib/rbac.ts` changes** (small, additive):
- Extend the `Area` union with `redditTemplates | companyInbox | companyMailboxes | clientsBasic | supportTickets | tasks`.
- Extend `AREA_ROLES` with entries for each (required by the `Record<Area, Role[]>` type — TypeScript enforces completeness, which is a good forcing function here): `redditTemplates: ["ADMIN"]`, `companyInbox: ["ADMIN"]`, `companyMailboxes: ["ADMIN"]`, `clientsBasic: ["ADMIN"]`, `supportTickets: ["SUPPORT","ADMIN"]` (exact parity with today's `support: ["SUPPORT","ADMIN"]`, so legacy SUPPORT-role behavior is unchanged), `tasks: ["SUPPORT","BILLING","ADMIN"]`.
- `HREF_AREA` changes: `"/admin/reddit"` and `"/admin/inbox"` and `"/admin/mailboxes"` move from `"platform"` to their new areas; `"/admin/support"` moves from `"support"` to the new, narrower `"supportTickets"`; add `"/admin/clients-basic": "clientsBasic"` and `"/admin/tasks": "tasks"`. Every other `platform`/`support` mapping (Settings, Staff, Audit, cold-email, ads, agency, SEO, domains, marketing, promotions, testimonials, chat, feedback, discord, …) is **left exactly as-is**.

**Action-file migrations** (each is a mechanical swap of the gate call, verified against the ground truth):
- `lib/actions-reddit-templates.ts`: all 14 `await requireAdmin();` calls → `await requireGrant("redditTemplates");`.
- `lib/actions-company-mail.ts`: `listCompanyMailboxes` and `listCompanyMailboxInfos` → `await requireAnyGrant(["companyInbox", "companyMailboxes"]);`; `createCompanyMailbox`, `createDefaultCompanyMailboxes`, `revealCompanyMailboxPassword`, `resetCompanyMailboxPassword`, `deleteCompanyMailbox` → `await requireGrant("companyMailboxes");` (these remain the more sensitive CRUD/credential-reveal operations, intentionally gated tighter than plain listing).
- `lib/mail/imap.ts`'s `resolveMailbox`: the existing `if (isStaff(user.role)) { … }` branch is **left untouched** for legacy roles (zero regression), and a new, additive condition is added so an `EMPLOYEE` only enters that branch when specifically granted: effectively `if (isStaff(user.role) || (user.role === "EMPLOYEE" && await hasAreaAccess(user, "companyInbox"))) { … }`. This closes a real gap I found: without this, granting `companyInbox` at the page level alone would be exactly the `lib/team-guard.ts` mistake (nav-visible but not enforced at the data layer), because `resolveMailbox` is the actual authority every mail action (`listFolders`, `listMessages`, `sendMessage`, `deleteMessage`, etc. in `lib/actions-mail.ts`) goes through.
- `lib/actions-support.ts`'s `requireTicketActor()`: change `isSupportStaff: canAccess(user.role, "support")` to `isSupportStaff: await hasAreaAccess(user, "supportTickets")`. This single change correctly threads through to `replyTicket`, `setTicketStatus`, and `writeTicketReply` (`lib/reply-core.ts`) — all of which already take `isSupportStaff`/`actorIsSupportStaff` as a passed-in boolean, so no other files change.
- `app/admin/reddit/page.tsx`, `app/admin/inbox/page.tsx`, `app/admin/mailboxes/page.tsx`, `app/admin/support/page.tsx`, `app/admin/support/[id]/page.tsx`: swap `requireArea("platform"/"support")` → `requireAreaOrGrant("redditTemplates"/"companyInbox"/"companyMailboxes"/"supportTickets")`.

**Structural test updates required in this same phase** (or CI breaks immediately, and correctly so):
- `test/company-mailbox.test.ts`: rewrite the `requireArea('platform')` assertion to assert `requireAreaOrGrant(["companyInbox","companyMailboxes"]-aware)` calls (adjust regex to match the new call patterns per-function, since list-functions and CRUD-functions now use different area strings); the `isStaff(user.role)` assertion in `resolveMailbox` still passes unmodified since that exact substring remains present; rewrite the final test's assertion from `/admin/mailboxes": "platform"` to `/admin/mailboxes": "companyMailboxes"`.
- `test/admin-actions-guards.test.ts`: add `"requireGrant("` and `"requireAnyGrant("` (and `"requireAreaOrGrant("` if any action file ever calls it directly) to both `AUTH_MARKERS` and `STAFF_MARKERS`. Add `actions-reddit-templates.ts` and `actions-company-mail.ts` to `ADMIN_ACTION_FILES` so the migration is actually exercised by this test rather than merely hoped-for (they weren't in that list before).
- `test/customer-actions-guards.test.ts`: update the doc-comment above the `requireTicketActor(` allowlist entry (lines ~186–190) — it currently says the helper "derives staff status from `canAccess(role, "support")`", which becomes inaccurate; update the prose to describe the new `hasAreaAccess(user, "supportTickets")`-based derivation. Not a hard test failure, but a correctness/documentation obligation given how deliberately this codebase's tests narrate *why* each guard is trusted.
- Run `npm test` after this phase — it is the fastest, cheapest way to prove no `platform`/`support` regression occurred anywhere else.

---

## Phase 3 — Admin-side "Staff" management UI (`/admin/staff`, ADMIN-only)

The route already exists (`app/admin/staff/page.tsx`, currently a simple role-promotion table backed by `lib/actions-staff.ts`'s `setUserRole`) and is already reserved in `lib/admin-groups.ts`'s nav under the `platform` area — it stays exactly that: `requireArea("platform")`, i.e. never manageable by anyone but ADMIN, per the explicit requirement.

**Rebuild scope:**
- Extend `app/admin/staff/page.tsx` (or split into `app/admin/staff/page.tsx` list + `app/admin/staff/[id]/page.tsx` detail, mirroring the existing `/admin/users` + `/admin/users/[id]` split) to add, per `EMPLOYEE`-role user:
  - **Create employee** flow — reuses the existing account-creation path (`Role.EMPLOYEE` instead of promoting an existing customer/staff row via `setUserRole`, since employees are typically brand-new accounts, not converted customers); a new action e.g. `createEmployee(email, name, tempPassword)` in a new/extended `lib/actions-staff.ts`.
  - **Grant checklist** — a form rendering one checkbox per grantable `Area` (`redditTemplates`, `companyInbox`, `companyMailboxes`, `clientsBasic`, `supportTickets`, `tasks`, and any future ones — driven by a single exported `GRANTABLE_AREAS: { area: Area; label: string; hint?: string }[]` array so adding a new grantable tool later is a one-line addition, not a UI rewrite). New actions `setStaffGrant(userId, area, granted: boolean)` upserting/deleting `StaffGrant` rows, each calling `requireAdmin()` (this file must never accept `requireGrant`/`requireAreaOrGrant` — granting grants is exclusively ADMIN's job, confirmed by the explicit requirement "must itself be ADMIN-only, never staff-manageable by other staff").
  - **IP whitelist configuration** — a small add/remove-row UI backed by `addStaffIp(userId, cidr, label?)` / `removeStaffIp(userId, id)` actions, validating input through a normalization helper (see Phase 4) before insert, both `requireAdmin()`-gated.
  - **Per-employee activity** — a link/embedded table reusing the audit viewer filtered to that employee (built in Phase 7), so the owner can jump from "this employee" straight to "everything they did."
- **New component** `components/admin/StaffGrantChecklist.tsx` (client component, mirrors the existing `StaffRoleControls.tsx` pattern) and `components/admin/StaffIpAllowlist.tsx`.
- `lib/actions-staff.ts` gains: `createEmployee`, `setStaffGrant`, `addStaffIp`, `removeStaffIp`, `listStaffGrants(userId)`, `listStaffIps(userId)` — all `requireAdmin()`-gated, each `revalidatePath("/admin/staff")` / the detail route, and each recording an audit entry (`staff.grant.add`, `staff.grant.remove`, `staff.ip.add`, `staff.ip.remove`, `staff.create`) via the shared audit helper built in Phase 7 (built here would be premature — Phase 3 can call the existing private `audit()`/`db.auditLog.create` inline for now, or better, sequence Phase 7's extraction earlier if the team wants to avoid double-touching this file; noted as a sequencing option below).

**Critical files:** `app/admin/staff/page.tsx`, new `app/admin/staff/[id]/page.tsx`, `lib/actions-staff.ts`, new `components/admin/StaffGrantChecklist.tsx`, new `components/admin/StaffIpAllowlist.tsx`.

---

## Phase 4 — Employee portal shell (`/staff`, new dedicated host)

Mirrors the *already-established* pattern in `app/admin/layout.tsx` almost exactly — that file already 404s the entire `/admin` tree unless the `Host` header matches `NXEON_ADMIN_HOSTS`, which is direct precedent for a third, separately-hosted portal.

**New file `app/staff/layout.tsx`:**
- `staffHostBlocked()` — identical shape to `adminHostBlocked()`, reading a new env var `NXEON_STAFF_HOSTS` (comma-separated), `notFound()` on mismatch, no restriction if unset (dev fallback) — exact copy of the existing function's logic and its documented fail-open-when-unset rationale.
- Auth gate: `realUser()`; redirect non-`EMPLOYEE`/non-`ADMIN` roles to `/dashboard` (CUSTOMER/SUPPORT/BILLING keep going to their existing homes, unaffected); allow `ADMIN` through too (so the owner can log into the employee portal to see exactly what an employee sees, for QA before granting something — cheap and valuable given the "over-exposure" risk called out in the constraints). Refuse impersonation exactly like `app/admin/layout.tsx` does (`if (imp) redirect(...)`) — impersonation is `ADMIN`-only to begin with and has no business in this portal.
- **Per-employee IP allowlist enforcement** — new function `staffIpBlocked(userId)` in a new file `lib/staff-ip.ts`, structurally parallel to `adminIpBlocked()` but scoped to one user's `StaffIpAllow` rows instead of the global `allowed_admin_ips` setting, reusing the same `clientIp()`-style header trust logic already centralized in `lib/rate-limit.ts` (extract `isPlainIp` out of `app/admin/layout.tsx` into a small shared exported helper, e.g. `lib/ip-format.ts`, imported by both the existing admin gate — unchanged behavior — and the new staff gate, so the literal-IP regex isn't duplicated). CIDR parsing reuses `normalizeCidr()` from the existing `lib/firewall-rules.ts` (already handles IPv4 CIDR validation/normalization for the server-firewall feature); a new small pure `ipInCidr(ip, cidr)` matcher is added alongside it for the runtime membership check (this doesn't exist yet — `normalizeCidr` only validates/normalizes for storage, it doesn't match).
  - **Fail-open/closed rule, exactly as specified**: if the employee has **zero** `StaffIpAllow` rows, access is unrestricted (fail open) — this prevents an admin who hasn't gotten to IP config yet from accidentally locking out a brand-new hire. The moment an admin adds even one row for that specific employee, the gate becomes fail-closed for that employee only (every other employee with no rows is unaffected). This mirrors `adminIpBlocked()`'s "malformed list fails open" philosophy but flips the trigger from "list is malformed" to "list is empty," which is the correct semantic for a per-user list that starts empty by construction.
- **Dynamic nav** — call `listGrantedAreas(user.id)` and map through a new, small `GRANTABLE_AREAS`-driven lookup (shared with Phase 3's checklist labels) to build a `NavSection[]` for the existing generic `Shell` component (`components/portal/Shell.tsx`, already used by both the customer dashboard and `/admin` via a `tag` prop — pass `tag="staff"` for this portal's own visual identity). Nav is **never hardcoded** — an employee with only `supportTickets` + `redditTemplates` granted sees exactly two nav entries, full stop.
- Staff 2FA enforcement — reuse the exact `enforce_staff_2fa` setting check already in `app/admin/layout.tsx` (cheap consistency win, no new setting needed).

**Login/session routing changes** (same unified session, no new auth system, per requirement):
- `lib/actions.ts` line ~417 (`redirect(next ?? (user.role === "ADMIN" ? "/admin" : "/dashboard"))`) and `app/login/page.tsx` line ~41 (identical ternary): extend to a small three-way `roleHome(role)` helper — `ADMIN → /admin`, `EMPLOYEE → /staff`, everything else → `/dashboard` — added once (e.g. in `lib/rbac.ts` or a tiny new `lib/portal-home.ts`) and used at both call sites, so `SUPPORT`/`BILLING`/`CUSTOMER` land exactly where they do today (no regression) and only the new role gets a new destination.

**Critical files:** new `app/staff/layout.tsx`, new `lib/staff-ip.ts`, new `lib/ip-format.ts` (extracted from `app/admin/layout.tsx`'s `isPlainIp`), `lib/firewall-rules.ts` (add `ipInCidr`), `lib/actions.ts` + `app/login/page.tsx` (redirect targets), `components/portal/Shell.tsx` (no structural change expected, just a new `tag` value).

---

## Phase 5 — Wire the five granted tools into the employee portal

For each of the four *existing* tools, extract the page body into a shared, chrome-agnostic view component so there is exactly one implementation reused by both `/admin/...` (unchanged data/behavior, just a swapped gate from Phase 2) and the new `/staff/...` route:

- `app/admin/support/page.tsx` body → `components/admin/SupportDeskView.tsx`; new `app/staff/support/page.tsx` calls `requireAreaOrGrant("supportTickets")` then renders it. Same for `app/admin/support/[id]/page.tsx` → a shared detail view, new `app/staff/support/[id]/page.tsx`.
- `app/admin/reddit/page.tsx` (already thin, 19 lines, delegates to `components/admin/RedditClient.tsx`) → duplicate the same ~10-line fetch-and-render body in `app/staff/reddit/page.tsx` with `requireAreaOrGrant("redditTemplates")`; given how thin this file already is, a shared-extraction wrapper is optional here — either approach is low-risk.
- `app/admin/inbox/page.tsx` (128 lines, delegates to `components/customer/mail/MailClient.tsx`) → extract into `components/admin/CompanyInboxView.tsx`, reused by `app/staff/inbox/page.tsx` (`requireAreaOrGrant("companyInbox")`).
- `app/admin/mailboxes/page.tsx` → extract into a shared view (or reuse `components/admin/CompanyMailboxes.tsx` directly, since it already looks like a self-contained client component), new `app/staff/mailboxes/page.tsx` (`requireAreaOrGrant("companyMailboxes")`).

**The fifth tool — new minimal Clients view — is built fresh, not extracted:**
- New file `app/staff/clients/page.tsx`, gated `requireAreaOrGrant("clientsBasic")`. Its Prisma query is the single most security-critical piece of this whole plan: it must `select` **only** `id, name, email, createdAt`, plus two `_count` aggregates (`tickets` and `servers` — both already exist as relations on `User`, confirmed in the schema: `tickets Ticket[]`, `servers Server[]`). No `balanceCents`, no wallet/transaction joins, no IP/geolocation history, no `AuditLog` relation, no internal notes, no impersonate action rendered anywhere in the component tree. This directly follows the principle already stated verbatim in this codebase's own `app/admin/users/[id]/page.tsx` comment: *"A control a role cannot use is not a permission, it is a promise the server refuses to keep."* — the server-side `select` clause is the actual enforcement; nothing about hiding fields client-side is acceptable here.

## Phase 6 — The "ClickUp alternative" task/project system

**MVP feature set** (data model already staged in Phase 1):
- Boards → columns (Kanban) → tasks, with drag-and-drop between columns and within a column (position-renumber strategy, reusing the exact "full-list-renumber on drop" approach already proven in `lib/actions-board.ts`/`components/admin/BoardClient.tsx`, rather than a fractional-index scheme — consistency with an existing, working pattern beats novelty here).
- Real assignment via `assigneeId` → `User`, due dates, priority (reusing `CardPriority`), checklist/sub-items, comments with real `authorId`, file attachments (reusing the existing on-disk-plus-metadata-row upload pattern from `CardAttachment`/its handling code, pointed at a separate upload directory so `WorkTaskAttachment` files are never mixed with the dev-ops board's).
- **One dependency decision**: adopt `dnd-kit` (small, well-maintained, no existing DnD library in the project) for the task board's drag-and-drop rather than hand-rolling native HTML5 drag events a second time — the existing `BoardClient.tsx` hand-rolled implementation is proven functional but is exactly the kind of code nobody wants to copy-paste-diverge a second time for a second board type; a shared drag primitive is worth the one new dependency here specifically because there will now be *two* Kanban UIs in the codebase.
- Routes: `/admin/tasks` (`requireArea("tasks")` variant — actually `requireAreaOrGrant("tasks")` so ADMIN/SUPPORT/BILLING keep unconditional access via `AREA_ROLES.tasks` and `EMPLOYEE` needs the grant) and `/staff/tasks`, sharing one `components/work/WorkBoardsView.tsx` + `components/work/WorkBoardClient.tsx`, exactly like the five tools above.
- New action file `lib/actions-work.ts` (`"use server"`), every export gated `requireAreaOrGrant("tasks")`, covering: create/rename/archive board & column, create/move/assign/prioritize/set-due-date/complete/archive task, add/toggle/delete checklist item, add comment, upload/delete attachment. Every mutating export also calls the shared audit helper from Phase 7 (`task.create`, `task.move`, `task.assign`, `task.comment`, `task.complete`, `task.checklist.toggle`, …) — this is the mechanism that makes "admin can see everything staff do in it" real rather than aspirational.
- Notifications: reuse the existing generic `Notification` model (already rendered by `Shell` in both portals) — assigning a task to someone, or commenting on a task they're assigned to, creates a `Notification` row with `href` pointing at `/staff/tasks/<id>` or `/admin/tasks/<id>` depending on the recipient's role. No new model needed for this.
- Admin oversight: `/admin/tasks` gets an "Activity" tab (or a dedicated `/admin/tasks/activity` route) that is really just the Phase-7 audit viewer pre-filtered to `action LIKE 'task.%'`, plus a lightweight "live-ish" refresh using the exact polling pattern already established by `components/admin/AdminChatNotifier.tsx` (an interval `fetch` against a small new API route, e.g. `/api/admin/tasks-unread` mirroring `/api/admin/chat-unread`) rather than introducing websockets — consistent with how "real-time" is already done elsewhere in this app.

**Explicit separation from the dev-ops board**: `lib/actions-work.ts` never imports from `lib/actions-board.ts`, `WorkTask` never references `Card`/`Board`, and nothing in the task system's action file is capable of invoking `runCardStageAction` or any of the deploy scripts (`publish-docs.mjs`, `deploy-staging.sh`, `promote-production.sh`) — those remain reachable only through `lib/actions-board.ts`'s hard `requireAdmin()` calls, untouched.

**Future ideas (explicitly out of MVP, captured for the owner's "what else belongs here" question):**
- Recurring tasks (a `recurrenceRule` on a task that spawns the next instance on completion).
- Time tracking / estimates (`estimatedMinutes` + start/stop timer rows, or simple manual time-logged entries per task).
- Calendar/timeline (Gantt-lite) view over `dueAt`.
- Task templates (a `WorkTaskTemplate` that pre-fills title/checklist/priority for repeatable work like "new employee onboarding" or "weekly Reddit posting round").
- Personal to-do lists distinct from team boards (a `personal: Boolean` flag or a fully separate lightweight model, scoped to `createdById === assigneeId` only).
- Workload/velocity dashboards (tasks completed per person per week, reusing the same audit trail as its source of truth rather than a separate counter).
- Saved filters/views (per-user saved query params, e.g. "my open tasks," "overdue across all boards").
- `@mentions` in comments, resolving to a `Notification`.
- Per-board membership/visibility (`WorkBoardMember`), once/if boards need to be restricted rather than visible to every `tasks`-granted user.

## Phase 7 — Comprehensive staff activity/audit visibility

**Extract a single shared, exported audit helper**, replacing the private, single-file `audit()` in `lib/actions.ts` (currently unexported, used by only ~19 call sites in that one file) and the scattered ad hoc `db.auditLog.create(...)` calls elsewhere:
- New file `lib/audit.ts` exporting `recordAudit(userId: string | null, action: string, detail?: string): Promise<void>`, with the *exact same body* as today's private `audit()` (including the impersonation-attribution logic reading `impersonating()` from `lib/auth.ts` and appending `actingAdmin=<id>`) — this is a pure extraction, zero behavior change.
- `lib/actions.ts` keeps working with a one-line `const audit = recordAudit;` alias, avoiding a 19-site rename inside that file.
- Every newly-migrated or newly-created staff-reachable action module imports `recordAudit` directly from `lib/audit.ts`: `lib/actions-work.ts` (all task mutations), `lib/actions-staff.ts` (grant/IP changes — already planned in Phase 3), and — as a follow-on cleanup, not blocking — the existing ad hoc `db.auditLog.create` call sites in `lib/actions-reddit-templates.ts`/`lib/actions-company-mail.ts` if any exist beyond what Phase 2 already touches, so that once an `EMPLOYEE` is using these tools, their actions are captured with the same consistency as everything else.

**`/opt/nxeon/app/admin/audit/page.tsx` enhancements:**
- Add a "Staff member" filter (`?staff=<userId>` query param, populated via a `<select>` of `Role.EMPLOYEE` users, extending the existing `db.auditLog.findMany` query with a `where: { userId: staffId }` clause) — directly answers "show me everything employee X did," per the requirement.

## Cross-cutting execution notes

- **Sequencing dependency**: Phase 3 (Staff management UI) technically needs Phase 1's schema and Phase 2's `hasAreaAccess`/`listGrantedAreas` to exist, but does *not* need Phase 4 (employee portal) to exist yet — the owner can create an employee and check off grants before the portal itself is live, which is a reasonable place to pause and demo progress. Phase 6 (tasks) is the most independent phase and could be built in parallel with Phases 3–5 by a second engineer, since it only depends on Phase 1's schema and Phase 2's `requireAreaOrGrant` primitive.
- **Staging-first, given the stated risk.** Per the project's own deploy workflow (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → `scripts/promote-production.sh`) and the explicit "a mistake here could over-expose customer data" concern: every phase from 2 onward should land on staging, get `npm test` run (the structural guard tests are the cheapest, fastest way to catch a permission regression), and get manually verified with a *real* `EMPLOYEE`-role test account (create one, grant exactly the four tools, verify the fifth/未-granted ones 403/redirect, verify `/admin/*` other `platform` tools are still unreachable) before `promote-production.sh` runs. This is especially important for Phase 2, since it is the one phase that edits already-shipped, already-tested production gates (`resolveMailbox`, `requireTicketActor`) rather than only adding new code.
- **`npm run db:push` timing**: run it once after Phase 1's schema lands, before any Phase 2+ code that reads `db.staffGrant`/`db.staffIpAllow`/`WorkTask` ships — matching the "stage the column before the code needs it" discipline already documented in this schema.
